---
title: "Dirac Notation — Vectors Written as Kets"
description: "A compact linear-algebra lesson with mathematical definitions, real values and reasoning."
---

## Start with a question

Quantum textbooks write |0⟩ rather than (1,0). Is that a different kind of object?

## Understand the central idea

A ket is a vector notation. Bras are dual vectors; inner products use a bra followed by a ket. The same vector and matrix intuition is being reused.

## Express it with mathematics

$$
|0\rangle=\begin{bmatrix}1\\0\end{bmatrix},\quad |1\rangle=\begin{bmatrix}0\\1\end{bmatrix}
$$

**Every symbol explained:** |0⟩ and |1⟩ are basis kets representing two standard basis vectors in a complex vector space. Square brackets contain coordinates; the ket symbol is a notation, not a new arithmetic operation.

**Substitute real numbers:** Combine them as (3/5)|0⟩+(4/5)|1⟩. The coordinate vector is (0.6,0.8). Its squared norm is 0.6²+0.8²=0.36+0.64=1, so it is normalised.

## Why this works

A qubit state is a unit vector of complex amplitudes. Basis states correspond to directions; measurements depend on squared magnitudes of the components in the chosen measurement basis.

## What can go wrong?

Quantum amplitudes may be complex. Their sum does not directly give a probability; use absolute-square magnitudes.

## Your turn

Take state (1/√2)|0⟩+(1/√2)|1⟩. Compute the probabilities for measuring 0 and 1.
